title: US PCE nowcast – Broadening pressures lock in December rate hike
author: Emma Pollard
text:
RESEARCH BRIEFING

16 Nov 2026

US PCE nowcast – Broadening pressures lock in December rate hike

Our monthly PCE nowcast provides an early estimate of inflation trends ahead of official data releases, highlighting key drivers and implications for Federal Reserve policy.

Our nowcast is for headline PCE inflation to rise to 3.8% y/y in October, up from 3.6% y/y in September. The details suggest high energy prices are lifting food inflation and bleeding into core inflation. This will be discomforting to the Federal Reserve and bolster our expectation for a 25bp rate hike at the December Federal Open Market Committee meeting; we think markets are overpricing the odds of a 50bp hike.

Recent declines in oil prices bode well for our forecast for headline inflation to peak in Q4, and the pass-through from higher energy prices to core inflation will ease over 2027. Muted equity markets, lower demand for homebuying, and modest wage growth should keep services inflation benign.

Each month, we replicate the Bureau of Economic Analysis’ (BEA) methodology to estimate the PCE deflator using the source data from the CPI, the PPI, and import prices. Because some underlying data and seasonal adjustments aren’t publicly available, there’s a small tracking error. Our average absolute errors since we began this approach are 3bps for headline and core PCE. Almost all the errors are in the core services ex-housing category, where the share of confidential data is the largest.
